Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manoj Kumar Srivastava,Pramod Kumar Srivastava
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant today, is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, learned counsel for the first informant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused involved in Case Crime No.33 of 2022, under Sections 363, 376 IPC, section 4 POCSO Act and section 3(2)V SC/ST Act,
P.S.Bahilpurwa, District Chitrakoot with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
Bachchharaj Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13909860/
1 4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Learned counsel has referred the statement of victim girl, recorded, under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C, and submitted that there are material contradictions in the statement of victim girl.

In her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.,
victim girl has inter-alia stated that her relative Sonu has dropped her outside the village of Parsaunja and while she was standing near a shop, applicant forcibly took her on a motorcycle,
whereas, in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., victim girl has stated that her relative Sonu has left her at Karvi and after that applicant met her at a shop and forcibly took her on his motorcycle.
At the time of her medical examination, victim has stated that after her relative Sonu has dropped her, she was sitting at a shop and from there she was forcibly taken away by applicant.
It was submitted that there are contradictions in the statement of victim and thus, her version is wholly unreliable.
It has also not be clarified that how the victim came to know about the name of applicant.
The ossification test of victim has not been conducted and as per school certificate, her age has been shown 17 years but in fact she is a major girl.

It was further submitted that applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 26.08.2022, having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and co-operate in the trial.

5. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the first informant have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that victim has made allegations that applicant has forcibly taken her on his motorcycle and committed rape upon her.
Her version is supported by her medical examination report.

It has also been shown that after incident, the police have reached at the spot and victim was brought by the police from the spot itself, whereas, applicant-accused has ran away and the motorcycle and mobile phone of applicant have been recovered near the spot of alleged incident.
As per school record, the age of victim is 17 years.

6. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, gravity of offence and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, the applicant-accused is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the bail application of applicant-accused is hereby rejected.

7. However, keeping in view of the period of incarceration of applicant-accused, the Trial Court is directed to expedite the trial and to decide the same, as early as possible, preferably within a period of nine months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, if there is no other legal impediment.

Order Date :- 18.5.2023 Neeraj  Bachchharaj Yadav vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13909860/
